overall_summary: Bitcoin is chopping near eighty-six thousand after a third rejection at eighty-seven K, with ETF outflows offset by steady corporate buying. Elevated yields and a firm dollar keep pressure on risk assets while soft jobs data limits hike odds. Geopolitical noise from Ukraine, Iran, and the Middle East adds uncertainty without a clear breakout catalyst.
key_points: BTC rejected at $87K again; range-bound near $86K
ETF $90M outflow vs Strive, Strategy, Metaplanet buys
10-year yield 5.35% and firm dollar weigh on crypto
Soft jobs hold Fed hike odds near 20%; minutes due
Geopolitical tensions elevated but unresolved for markets

items.title: Bitcoin Rejected at $87K for Third Time
items.summary: Bitcoin got turned away from just above eighty-seven thousand dollars again on Monday, the third rejection since late September, and slipped back toward the eighty-five six to eighty-six thousand zone. Rising Treasury yields near multi-decade highs are capping risk assets even as Nasdaq hits records and soft jobs data has dialed down October Fed hike odds. Traders should watch the tightening triangle of higher lows versus that hard resistance; a clean break higher needs stronger spot demand, while a slip under eighty-four thousand risks a faster move toward eighty thousand.
items.impact: Range-bound volatility until $87k break or support failure

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Post $90M Outflow Monday
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs flipped to roughly ninety million dollars in net outflows on October fifth after two solid inflow days, with only BlackRock's IBIT still taking money while Ark and Fidelity saw heavy redemptions. Cumulative inflows sit near fifty-eight billion and assets around one hundred eleven billion, but the daily reverse comes as Bitcoin trades about thirty-two percent below its October twenty twenty-five all-time high. Traders care because ETF flows are the cleanest daily read on institutional spot demand; another red day or two would pressure the bid under this range.
items.impact: Weaker near-term institutional bid and possible selling pressure

items.title: Strive Buys 2,000 BTC; Strategy Adds 334
items.summary: Nasdaq-listed Strive disclosed its largest Bitcoin purchase since June, picking up two thousand coins for about one hundred sixty-nine million dollars last week and lifting holdings to roughly twenty-nine thousand four hundred sixty-two BTC. Strategy, the biggest corporate holder, added another three hundred thirty-four Bitcoin for nearly twenty-nine million, bringing its stack to eight hundred forty-eight thousand. These treasury buys keep corporate demand alive even while ETF flows wobble, giving traders a counterweight to short-term outflows and reinforcing the narrative that large holders still accumulate on dips.
items.impact: Sustained corporate accumulation supports downside protection

items.title: Metaplanet Nets +1,000 BTC to 44,000 Holdings
items.summary: Japanese Bitcoin treasury firm Metaplanet sold ten thousand Bitcoin then bought eleven thousand in the third quarter, ending with a net one-thousand-coin increase and forty-four thousand BTC total, making it the second-largest public corporate holder behind Strategy. The round-trip was framed as a liquidity demonstration for credit rating agencies and future bond or preferred financing while keeping Bitcoin as eighty-five to ninety percent of assets. Traders should note the continued corporate stacking and the willingness to rotate for balance-sheet optics without abandoning the core treasury thesis.
items.impact: Reinforces corporate Bitcoin adoption and second-tier treasury demand

items.title: Crypto Liquidations Hit $160M–$194M, Longs Hit Harder
items.summary: Over the past day crypto derivatives saw roughly one hundred sixty to one hundred ninety-four million dollars liquidated across more than sixty thousand traders, with longs taking the larger share as Bitcoin faded from the eighty-seven thousand test. The biggest single hit was an eleven-plus million dollar Bitcoin position on Binance; open interest and funding stayed relatively stable rather than cascading. For traders this is classic range chop flushing leverage on both sides instead of a directional wipeout, so watch whether funding cools further or OI rebuilds into the next push.
items.impact: Leverage reset in range; limited directional follow-through expected

items.title: Smaller Alts Outperform as BTC Chops Near $86K
items.summary: While Bitcoin and the majors stayed range-bound near eighty-six thousand, smaller names led gains with Bitway's BTW jumping about twenty-five percent, Filecoin and LayerZero double-digit, and Cardano up roughly eleven percent. Derivatives open interest held steady near twenty-two billion with cooler funding and only modest liquidations. Traders should care because capital is rotating into higher-beta names rather than exiting crypto entirely; if Bitcoin finally clears eighty-seven thousand this rotation can accelerate, but a BTC breakdown would likely reverse the alt strength quickly.
items.impact: Selective risk-on in alts while BTC leadership remains unresolved

items.title: 10-Year Yield Hits 5.35%, Multi-Decade Highs
items.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield climbed to around 5.31 to 5.35 percent on Monday, its highest close since 2002, with the 30-year also pushing toward 5.66 to 5.70 percent. This happened even as odds of an October Fed hike fell sharply after the soft jobs report. Higher long-term yields raise the cost of capital across the board and often pressure risk assets including Bitcoin because they compete with equities and crypto for investor money. Traders should watch whether yields keep climbing or pull back ahead of the FOMC minutes.
items.impact: Higher discount rates and tighter financial conditions weigh on crypto and risk assets

items.title: ISM Services Prices Paid Surge to 74
items.summary: September ISM Services PMI eased to 54.9 from 55.4, still solidly in expansion, but the prices paid index jumped to 74.0, the highest since July 2022. Employment ticked back into expansion while new orders and activity cooled a bit. Sticky services inflation and stretched supply chains keep the Fed's dual mandate complicated. For crypto traders this is a hawkish signal that could limit how far rate-cut hopes run and support higher yields.
items.impact: Reinforces sticky inflation narrative, limiting dovish Fed repricing

items.title: Soft Jobs Keep October Fed Hike Odds Near 20%
items.summary: Friday's September payrolls of just plus 29,000 with big downward revisions and unemployment at 4.2 percent continue to dominate the macro conversation. Wage growth slowed to 3.0 percent year-over-year. Markets now see only about a 20 to 25 percent chance of another hike at the late-October FOMC, down from over 70 percent a week earlier. Softer labor data reduces near-term tightening risk, which is generally supportive for Bitcoin and risk assets if inflation does not reaccelerate.
items.impact: Lowers near-term rate-hike probability, easing policy pressure on risk assets

items.title: Dollar Index Holds Firm Near 102 on High Yields
items.summary: The U.S. Dollar Index closed Monday around 102.17, near recent highs, and remains supported Tuesday by elevated Treasury yields despite softer Fed hike odds. A strong dollar typically acts as a headwind for Bitcoin and other risk assets priced in dollars. Crypto traders should note the divergence: front-end rate expectations softened but the long end and the dollar stayed bid, keeping financial conditions tighter than pure rate-path pricing suggests.
items.impact: Stronger USD creates headwind for dollar-denominated crypto prices

items.title: FOMC Minutes Due Wednesday After September Hike
items.summary: Markets are focused on Wednesday's release of the minutes from the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, when the Fed raised rates by 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00 percent. The minutes will show how much urgency officials felt for further hikes and how they weighed inflation risks versus the labor market. With October hike odds already low, any language leaning patient or data-dependent could reinforce the pause narrative, while hawkish details could reprice yields higher again.
items.impact: Key catalyst for near-term rate path and yield volatility ahead of late-October meeting

items.title: Eurozone Retail Sales Edge Up; US Trade Data Due
items.summary: Eurozone retail sales rose a mild 0.1 percent month-over-month in August, missing the 0.2 percent forecast, while year-over-year growth was 0.8 percent. Separately, the full U.S. goods and services trade balance for August is scheduled for release today after the advance goods deficit already widened sharply to 132.6 billion dollars. Soft European consumption is mildly negative for global growth sentiment, and a wider U.S. trade gap would reinforce the drag on third-quarter GDP. Crypto traders watch these for broader risk appetite and dollar moves.
items.impact: Mild data points; wider US deficit could weigh on growth views and USD dynamics

items.title: Yemen Forces Push Houthis from Bab el-Mandeb Strait
items.summary: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces launched a major offensive and claim to have driven Iran-aligned Houthis from key positions around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the port of Mocha. Pakistan and Turkey pledged troops under a joint defence pact while Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes on Riyadh airport and Aramco sites. Traders should care because this chokepoint handles huge Red Sea oil and trade flows that Saudi Arabia has been using to bypass Hormuz risks. Any sustained disruption or wider Iran proxy war keeps energy prices elevated and pressure on risk assets.
items.impact: Heightened Red Sea shipping and oil supply risk

items.title: Ukraine Hits Moscow Region with 650 Drones
items.summary: Ukraine launched one of its largest drone assaults in years on the Moscow region overnight, with Russian officials reporting around 650 drones, two deaths, damaged homes and a fire at a major fuel depot supplying Moscow airports. Russia claimed nearly 900 drones intercepted across regions while Ukraine continues striking Russian refining capacity, recently claiming over half is offline. This escalates the energy war that has already tightened global diesel and oil product supplies. Crypto and risk traders watch it because further hits on Russian energy infrastructure support higher energy prices and inflation pressure.
items.impact: Tighter refined products supply and risk-off pressure

items.title: Iran Holds Hormuz Closed; G7 Releases Oil Stocks
items.summary: Iran’s parliament speaker said the Strait of Hormuz will stay restricted until the US meets seven conditions from earlier talks, while tanker attacks continue. G7 nations agreed to release 100 million barrels of crude and diesel from strategic reserves over coming months, and Middle East crude exports have recovered toward or above pre-war levels on some days. Oil hovered near 100 dollars a barrel with some easing. For traders this is the core energy shock of 2026: any fresh disruption spikes inflation and yields, while successful releases and flows can ease pressure on risk assets.
items.impact: Oil volatility still high but supply relief attempts underway

items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Leads Brazil First-Round Vote
items.summary: Right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, took about 47 percent in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election, ahead of incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva at roughly 45 percent. A runoff is set for October 25 and markets reacted strongly with the Bovespa surging nearly 9 percent. The result signals a sharp rightward shift in Latin America’s largest economy. Traders care because Brazil is a major emerging-market and commodities player; a Bolsonaro win is widely seen as more market-friendly on fiscal and regulatory grounds.
items.impact: EM risk appetite lift and Brazil asset rally

items.title: US Pulls Bombers from UK Base over Iran Threat
items.summary: The United States rapidly withdrew all its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in Britain after intelligence of a potential Iranian drone-style attack on the base, following earlier arrests linked to a suspected plot. President Trump confirmed threats he linked to Iran and said the aircraft were moved for safety. The base had been a key forward location for strikes related to the Iran conflict. This underscores ongoing escalation risk in the US-Iran war and keeps geopolitical premium in energy and defense markets elevated.
items.impact: Signals persistent Iran conflict escalation risk

items.title: Spain’s Sánchez Calls Snap Election for November 29
items.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap general election for November 29 after parliament rejected his emergency housing decrees amid nationwide protests over rents and evictions. Polls currently favour the centre-right People’s Party, possibly needing far-right Vox support to govern. The euro has been under pressure from European fiscal and political stress. For markets this adds another layer of political uncertainty in the eurozone at a time of already high bond yields and energy-driven inflation worries.
items.impact: Elevated eurozone political risk and euro pressure
